title: Evening Compline
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Wednesday Morning's Breakfast Rides  Casual Pace Variable Distance RSVP
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
Every Wednesday morning...Ride and eat Yummy breakfast together.

Please do not go on this ride unless you will ride at a casual pace and stay with the group . We will meet to ride to breakfast at a casual pace. After eating some may split up with some returning to the start and others going longer and faster.
Helmets are mandatory; No ear buds or audible music playing devices. Please bring water, and a basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).
To eliminate passing around a pen and paper waiver, we encourage LBC Club membership and Meetup RSVP below to join this ride. RSVP also allows us to contact you after the ride if needed. If you do not RSVP you are not covered by the club excess accident insurance policy; only club members who RSVP are covered. Being on Meetup does not mean you are a club member. via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: SACA Fiesta
location: Vue De La Lune, 360 Weaver Rd, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17603, United States
description:
SACA Fiesta is an annual cultural celebration that brings together community members, supporters, and partners to celebrate Latino heritage while supporting the work of SACA Broadcasting- WLCH FM. The event features live musica, traditional cuisine, cultural performances, and opportunities to connect with community leaders and organizations.
SACA Fiesta not only highlights the richness and diversity of Latino culture but also serves as an important fundraiser that helps sustain WLCH’s programs dedicated to education, community development, and access to vital resources.
Our theme this year is “The 80’s”- a decade that shaped a generation and continues to influence today’s leaders, innovators and changemakers. For many, the 1980’s were not only a time of cultural explosion and bold expression, but also a moment when the Latino community in the United States began gaining stronger visibility and making meaningful strides in public life, education, business, and the arts.
At this year’s Fiesta, we want to celebrate how Latinos have embraced and contributed to the American cultural landscape, while also recognizing the opportunities this country continues to offer our community. From fashion to music, from food to iconic moments in history, the 80’s will come alive with joy, rhythm, and pride.

* **Route:** Expect a total distance of approximately **15-20 miles**, including **3-4 loops** of a circuit featuring **1-2 climbing segment**.

title: LBC Bike to 30K Program: Ride #2 Pedal to Preserve
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
**Grab your helmets, bikes, and sneakers — Lancaster Bicycle Club is gearing up for beginner and transitional rides!** Local members of the LBC are thrilled to host this year’s **Bike to 30K Program**, designed especially for new, returning, and curious cyclists.

## **About the Program**

Bike to 30K is a seven‑week series that gently builds your confidence, fitness, and mileage. We begin with a five‑mile ride and gradually work up to eighteen miles by the end of the program. Our goal is simple: to introduce riders of all experience levels to the joy of cycling in a supportive, community‑focused environment.
This program is **FREE** with an LBC membership — and membership is also free. The Bike to 30K program is open to everyone in our community who wants to ride.

## **Why We Ride**

Ever wonder why cyclists keep coming back? Because it’s fun. There’s nothing like coasting downhill and letting out a big “weeeeeee” all the way to the bottom. But we also know that if you’re new to cycling, jumping straight into an 18‑mile ride can feel intimidating. That’s exactly why Bike to 30K exists.
Each week, you’ll increase your mileage at a comfortable pace. You’ll get to know the club, meet fellow riders, and gradually grow into a confident **Fun Rider** — the group known for enjoying scenic, social rides together.

## **Our Commitment to You**

Lancaster Bicycle Club is dedicated to supporting new riders and helping our community reach their cycling goals. Bike to 30K is part of our initiative to encourage more people to get outside, get active, and discover how enjoyable cycling can be.
Spend seven weeks with us and watch yourself transform into a Fun Rider — one mile at a time.
The Bike to 30K program is voluntary, welcoming, and designed with beginners in mind. We can’t wait to ride with you.

## **Membership, Waiver & RSVP Requirements**

To eliminate passing around a pen‑and‑paper waiver, we require both:

* **LBC Club Membership**, and
* **Meetup RSVP**

Your RSVP allows us to contact you after the ride if needed. Please note: **ONLY club members who RSVP are covered by the club’s excess accident insurance policy.** Being on Meetup does *not* mean you are a club member. To join our wonderful club, please sign up through our membership link.

## **Before You Arrive**

Please plan to arrive **10–15 minutes before the ride** and ensure your bike is in good working condition. Helmets are mandatory. Please also bring:

* 1–2 water bottles
* A basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump or CO₂ inflator)

For everyone’s safety, **earbuds and music are not allowed**.

## **RSVP Required**

Your RSVP is your agreement to follow:

* The club’s **Code of Conduct**
* The **Rules of the Road**
* Our **Ride Waiver**

## **Stay Connected**

We’ve gone social! Join us on Facebook: **https://www.facebook.com/B230K**

## **What to Bring**

Water bottle • Bike • Helmet • Sneakers
Cue Sheet to the Ride: [Ride #2 Pedal to Preserve ](https://routes.lancasterbikeclub.net/cue/gsv-pedal-to-preserve-short-6r/)

***The Bike to 30K is brought to you by Lancaster Bicycle Club and Lancaster Trek Bikes.***

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: Introduction to bikepacking 101 (37 R)
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
Ride Leader: Bruce Black

An introduction to bikepacking. This is a 37-mile route with an overnight camping experience at Starlight campground in Clay, PA. We will start in Lititz with a gear check and loading onto bicycles. From Lititz, we will make our way to Foxmill Creamery (about 10 miles into the ride) in Clay for an afternoon snack. From there, we will head into the gamelands for some gravel riding as we make our way to the campsite at roughly the 20-mile mark. **YOU WILL WANT TO RIDE A BIKE THAT IS CAPABLE OF RIDING ON GRAVEL.** After a restful night of sleeping under the stars, we will pack up and head back to Lititz, stopping at a coffee shop along the way. Plan on cooking a meal for dinner and for breakfast. This will test out your campsite cooking setup and food choices. Please check out the [Bikepacking 101 gear list](https://bikepacking.com/bikepacking-101/pack-list/) for some ideas on what to bring and how to set up your bike. Another good reference is the following YouTube video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zH4NOPWZxGU](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zH4NOPWZxGU)

**ALL RIDERS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THEIR OWN GEAR AND FOOD. YOU ARE GOING TO WANT A GRAVEL BIKE FOR THIS RIDE.**

The idea of this trip is to test out the gear setup on the bike and camping in preparation for riding the Great Allegheny Passage and C&O Canal paths from Pittsburgh to Washington, DC.

If you have any questions please message me.

This ride is a social ride, but cyclists are not expected to stay in one group. Cyclists may pedal at their own comfortable paces. Please be supportive of the other cyclists to avoid anyone biking alone or being dropped off the back of the last group.

description:
Dorian Blue Jazz is dedicated to bringing classic jazz standards to life with warmth, swing, and timeless elegance. Featuring Bill Druck on guitar and Bryan Hoke on saxophone, the group channels the relaxed sophistication and lyrical interplay of the iconic Jim Hall/Paul Desmond recordings. The combo is rounded out by a guest bassist, with different bassists appearing from performance to performance—adding variety, spontaneity, and fresh musical interplay each time they take the stage. 
Bill and Bryan share a deep love for the Great American Songbook, delivering performances that are both intimate and engaging, making Dorian Blue Jazz an ideal accompaniment to your dinner at the Log Cabin restaurant. 
The duo’s musical connection goes back decades. Bill and Bryan originally performed together as Dorian Blue in the 1980s, developing a tight musical rapport and shared vision for jazz rooted in melody and feel. After a long hiatus, they’ve reunited, picking up right where they left off—playing together as if they never missed a beat. With experience, chemistry, and a rotating lineup of guest bassists, Dorian Blue Jazz offers a sound that is both nostalgic and fresh.

title: Leonid & Friends
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $44 $54 $64 $74
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, September 24, 2025 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, September 26, 2025 at 10:00 a.m. 
With multiple sold-out U.S. tours under its belt and hundreds of thousands of fans around the world, Leonid & Friends continues to astound its global audience with its unique ability in capturing the spirit, musicality, and fire of American supergroup Chicago. 
And what is even more stunning is that Leonid & Friends, comprised of 11 of the finest musicians in Russia, haven’t seen Chicago perform live until recently, yet replicates the band’s complex arrangements amazingly note for note. Chicago has never been in Russia, and none of us have attended their concerts until just recently in the United States,” said Leonid Vorobyev, a multi-instrumentalist who is the band’s leader. “We have only recordings and videos (to help us learn Chicago songs).” 
Ironically, Vorobyev wasn’t always a fan of horn bands, and as a teenager gravitated to the hard-driving guitar-based sounds of the Beatles, Creedence Clearwater Revival, Deep Purple, and Grand Funk Railroad. “In the early 1970s in the USSR, electric guitars, amplifiers, and drums were rare to find so at school we were playing self-made instruments,” Vorobyev explained. “We were allowed to rehearse in the same room with a horns band. Those musicians almost always were drunk and quite often tried to play with us our rock songs. It was a nightmare, and I hated them all!” 
But that all changed when Vorobyev heard Chicago. He became an instant fan. “I loved so much the brilliant mixture of rock guitars, drums, and jazz horns with bright vocal harmonies,” he said.
In 2014, Vorobyev decided to indulge his love for the band by gathering a few fellow musicians in a studio to record a video of them playing his favorite Chicago tune, Brand New Love Affair. No charts or scores of the song existed so Vorobyev transcribed the tune by ear. The result was a YouTube video that quickly went viral. Since then Leonid & Friends has recorded videos of other Chicago hits including Make Me Smile, 25 or 6 to 4, and Saturday In The Park. 
All total the videos have received more than 50 million views. Also, Leonid & Friends has recorded two albums showcasing its tribute to Chicago. In September of 2018, the band recorded its first song from legendary supergroup Earth, Wind, & Fire and also paid tribute to the band Blood, Sweat & Tears as well. 
Borrowing a line from one of Chicago’s biggest hits, “it’s only the beginning” of great things from Leonid & Friends. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: 2026 Open Streets Lancaster
location: North/Sout Water Street, South Water Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Lancaster Rec’s 11th Annual Open Streets Lancaster event will temporarily close Water Street to motorized vehicles and open them to the Lancaster community. Our Lancaster event joins more than 130 Open Streets initiatives in the United States and Canada.

Open Streets Lancaster is different than a block party or street fair. It is part of a broad effort to encourage physical activity, re-imagine the City as a place to walk and bike for transportation, help people meet, and steward meaningful social connections.

Hosted by Lancaster Rec and held in partnership with City of Lancaster and the Lancaster Bikes program, Open Streets Lancaster is a free family-friendly event that temporarily transforms Water Street into a paved playground. Pedestrian traffic replaces car traffic and people of all ages, abilities and backgrounds can uncover new interests, discover their talents and improve their general well-being.

The route features activities promoting physical and mental health, as well as local bands and musicians, artists, food trucks and opportunities to learn about non-profits and small businesses.

Our event reimagines transportation and community connections throughout the City of Lancaster. Attendees are encouraged to walk, bike, blade, and skate to the event and to meaningfully meet their neighbors.

location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:

Herman’s Hermits
British Invasion icon Peter Noone—the unmistakable voice of Herman’s Hermits—brings a hit-packed evening of songs, stories, and good-natured humor. Backed by his seasoned band, Noone revisits the soundtrack of the 1960s with favorites like “I’m Into Something Good,” “Mrs. Brown, You’ve Got a Lovely Daughter,” “There’s a Kind of Hush,” “I’m Henry VIII, I Am,” “Silhouettes,” and more. Expect crisp harmonies, jangly guitars, and the playful stage presence that’s endeared him to fans across generations. Between songs, Peter shares crowd-pleasing anecdotes from the road and the heyday of the British Invasion, turning the concert into an intimate, feel-good celebration of timeless pop. Whether you grew up with these classics or you’re discovering them for the first time, this sing-along night will leave you smiling—a joyful trip back to the golden age of ’60s pop with a performer who still makes it feel brand new.
 
Chris Ruggiero
Contemporary crooner Chris Ruggiero brings the spirit of the ’60s and ’70s to life in a shimmering, feel-good concert of timeless pop. Backed by a crack band and lush arrangements, Chris leans into the romance, rhythm, and melody of the era, delivering fresh takes that honor the originals while letting his smooth, soaring vocals shine. description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

description:
Exploring Greenfield’s Restored Meadows: A Guided Nature Walk
 
Meadows are among the most vibrant and diverse ecosystems, alive with color and activity. Join us for a guided hike with the Lancaster Conservancy through Greenfield’s restored meadows and experience the beauty and abundance of life they support. From native wildflowers to pollinators like butterflies and bees, these habitats showcase the incredible connections within nature.

This slow-paced walk is perfect for anyone who enjoys observing the details of the natural world. Along the way, we’ll discuss the restoration process, the species that thrive here, and why meadows are essential for biodiversity.

Event Highlights:

– A leisurely hike through Greenfield’s restored meadows
– Opportunities to see native flowers and pollinators up close
– Insights into meadow ecology and restoration efforts
 

Details:

– Easy, slow-paced hike
– Dress for the weather and bring drinking water
– Suitable for ages 5 and up

description:
Creative Playground is a hands-on, come-and-go community art event celebrating imagination, collaboration, and making together as families hosted by the Center for Creative Exploration at Pennsylvania College of Art & Design along with community partners. This event takes place 3:30 – 6 pm

The Center for Creative Exploration at Pennsylvania College of Art & Design will be hosting a giant making table open for the full duration—inviting artists of all ages to tinker, build, and create freely. Peace Kids to the Rescue will guide children and adults through a collaborative monoprinting experience using cake pans and paints.

Geared toward children ages 2–10 and their caregivers—but welcoming creators of all ages—this activity emphasizes teamwork and storytelling through building. 

And beginning at 4:30 pm, Hillside Place Studio will offer a quieter, low-key mixed media experience inspired by the book We Share This Neighborhood. Through collage, assemblage, and experimentation, participants will reflect on ideas of neighborhood and belonging, creating small works that express what community means to them in a calm, welcoming space.

Join us for a playful, process-focused evening of activities designed to encourage shared creativity between adults and kids. 

This event is free and open to the public. Please register so we know how much fun to have on hand! RSVP Link: https://forms.gle/pvXmjr3TzzTfXxEE8

title: Farm to Fork Experience
location: Bird-in-Hand Village Inn & Suites, 2695 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA, 17505, United States
description:
Real Farms • Real Food
May 13, 2026
Food doesn’t get any more authentic than Bird-in-Hand’s Farm-to-Fork Experience. From milking cows to making ice cream to growing chemical-free produce from seed, you’ll meet Mennonite and Amish farmers and get an intimate view of how Lancaster County’s bounty begins. Our own John Smucker, an eighth-generation farmer, will be your guide on this unforgettable experience, which culminates in a mouth-watering farm-to-fork meal. 
The Farm to Fork Experience package includes:
• Two-night stay in the historic Bird-in-Hand Village Inn & Suites
• Tours of local farms and a lunch made with ingredients from our tour – see itinerary below
• Daily deluxe continental breakfasts for two at the Village Inn & Suites or credit at the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe
• Dinner for two at the Bird-in-Hand Family Restaurant & Smorgasbord on Tuesday or Wednesday
• Welcome market basket filled with local foods 
Space is limited so reserve early. Enjoy this package for $585 (plus tax). Extend your stay for only $109 a night (plus tax). For more information on the Village Inn & Suites, click here. Walking is required for these tours. 
Requires $200 deposit to reserve your tour (refundable up to two weeks prior to event). $109 extra night available for any room type. Taxes not included. 
  
2026 TOUR ITINERARY 
Rise, Shine & Dine (5:30 am): Wake up with the roosters and see cows being milked at our neighbor Aaron Lantz’s organic farm. Then savor a delicious farm-fresh breakfast with the Lantz family in their kitchen. 
Hydroponic Farming: At Millcreek Hydroponics, we’ll learn about the sustainable year-round growing methods for their lettuce and microgreens, and tour their greenhouse. 
The Time is Ripe: Take an orchard tour of Kauffman’s Fruit & Farm Market and learn how they produce their apple cider. 
Veggies on the Vine: Amish farmer Ephraim Huyard will show us his biological methods of growing plants, and how he grows the chemical-free vegetable plants. 
Growing Green: Meet Wesley Groff, third-generation farmer of Groff’s Celery and Vegetable Farm, and learn how he grows crops from seed in a chemical-free environment. 
Grown Local Luncheon: You’ve seen where it’s grown. Now taste the fresh difference. Receive a market basket of local foods after lunch. 
Save Room for Dessert: Our last stop after lunch will be a visit to the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe, where we make our artisan ice cream.

Come out and enjoy a great night of live music, artistic expression, and delicious drinks – highlighting the incredible talent in our backyard! 
Featuring Local Artists – Johnny Zarfati, Dylan Zangwill, Barkley Cove, & Easy Brother 
Johnny Zarfati
Johnny Zarfati is a New Jersey based Americana artist. He draws on the grit of the northeast and the soul of American roots music to craft a sound that feels both “lived in” and fresh. Blending Folk, Americana, and alt country his music searches for something real. Part Troubadour, part poet, grounded in tradition but unafraid to carve his own path.
Website | Instagram 
Dylan Zangwill
In 2022, Dylan traveled to Nashville where he worked with Grammy Award-Winning producer John Carter Cash at the legendary Cash Cabin, recording 4 of Dylan’s original songs. Late in 2022, Dylan appeared on American Idol Season 21 where he amazed the judges with an original composition, “Bittersweet Melody” and received his Golden Ticket to Hollywood.  Following Idol, he went back to the studio to record more originals, this time with producer Adam Weiner and the backing of Adam’s band, Low Cut Connie. He’s performed at venues of all sizes throughout the Philadelphia metro area and has also taken the show on the road to Delaware, Maryland, Nashville, New Orleans, Los Angeles, Hollywood, Austin, Florida, New York, and even London audiences. Dylan’s signature sound is unmistakable: powerful vocals, refined piano and guitar playing, and enthralling originals, delivered with a unique and engaging blend of bluesy rock and Southwestern flair.
Website | Instagram | Facebook 
Barkley Cove
Barkley Cove is the band to watch in the new folk scene. Raised on collaborative songwriting, rich vocal harmony, and the folk revival records of the 60s and beyond, members Jillian Dolan (guitar), Yusuf Miller (mandolin), Silas Gross (banjo), and Robert Myers (bass) mix genres of folk, rock, country, and bluegrass to create a distinctly original sound that will linger in your ear long after the last chord. As their reach expands throughout the United States, Barkley Cove’s imaginative songwriting and dedication to originality continue to push the boundaries of new folk music.

With the allure of a modern day outlaw, Gary Allan has won over fans, peers, and critics with his signature blend of smoldering vocals, rebellious lyrics, and raucous live performances. #### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
May 30, June 13, June 27, July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

Featuring Tracy Locke, Avery Quinn, & Sean Morton!  
Since 1956, Warwick Community Ambulance has proudly served Lititz and the surrounding communities with 24/7 emergency medical care. Every dollar raised through this comedy night stays right here at home, supporting local ambulances, equipment, training, and the providers who respond when our neighbors need help. By buying a ticket, you are directly investing in the care of your community and helping ensure Warwick EMS is ready when it matters most. 
Tracy Locke
Take the all American girl next door, add a pinch of devilish charm, a dash of sports fanatic, some raw charisma, sprinkle in kooky, eclectic characters set on high speed and POW! the perfect recipe for comedy. Tracy Locke has been performing as a professional comedian for over 18 years, from sold out shows at Radio City Music Hall to comedy clubs across the nation. She has hosted television, live events and award shows as well as co-founding the corporate training company Productively Funny which specializes in custom-made, interactive corporate training workshops. 
Avery Quinn
Avery Quinn is a comedian originally from Lititz, PA, now residing in Hartford, CT. He was the winner of the 2024 Last Comix Standing contest at Comix Roadhouse at Mohegan Sun Casino. Avery has been making audiences laugh since 2018 with his physical comedy and absurd observations all across the East Coast.  He has headlined at Comix Roadhouse at Mohegan Sun, the BrewHaha in Wethersfield CT, City Winery in New York and Western New England University.  Avery has featured at various comedy clubs and colleges including New York Comedy Club Stamford, Stress Factory in Bridgeport CT, Dojo of Comedy in New Jersey, and UCONN.  He was also a featured performer at the Portland Maine Comedy Festival and a semifinalist in the 2020 Philly’s Phunniest Comic contest at Helium Comedy Club.  Avery has made appearances on Investigation Discovery and Oxygen Network. 
Sean Morton
A veteran road comic for over 17 years, Sean has performed at clubs and casinos across the US, was a member of the legendary Friars Club, and released his first stand-up special in 2024, which landed in the top 10 of the comedy charts.

title: Dick Fox’s Golden Boys starring Frankie Avalon and Fabian with special guest Tommy Cono Tributing Bobby Rydell
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $69 $79 $89 $99 
Relive the magic of the golden era of rock ‘n’ roll with Dick Fox’s Golden Boys! This unforgettable concert event reunites beloved teen idols of the late 1950s and early 1960s — Frankie Avalon and Fabian, with special guest Tommy Cono (tributing Bobby Rydell) — for an evening packed with timeless hits, charm, and nostalgia. 
From Avalon’s chart-topping favorites like “Venus” and “Why” to Fabian’s energetic classics including “Turn Me Loose” and “Tiger,” audiences will be transported back to a time when rock ‘n’ roll ruled the airwaves. With the addition of Tommy Cono’s smooth vocals and dynamic stage presence, this show is a celebration of music that defined a generation. 
Dick Fox’s Golden Boys blends unforgettable songs, stories, and humor into a joyful trip down memory lane — reminding us why these performers became household names and fan favorites around the world. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

There will be a Q&A session following where audience members are encouraged to ask questions. All ages welcome. Registration RequestedCortney Dean is a Conservation Biologist and Independent Researcher living in Northern Wisconsin. She studies how beavers impact ecosystems- including other animals like bats and birds, water quality, food webs, and biodiversity. Outside of her research, Cortney enjoys reading, gardening, hiking, canoeing, rockhounding, and adventures with her spouse and two dogs.

location: Church of the Apostles UCC, 1850 Marietta Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Join us for our May 21, 2026 Mocktails & Meaning™ gathering for a powerful and eye-opening conversation led by Brad Ortenzi, Eastern USA Regional Director of ZOE International and Coordinator of the Berks and Lancaster County Human Trafficking Task Forces. Drawing on his experience as a former Ephrata Police Detective, his work with federal and county child exploitation task forces, and his international work combating trafficking in Thailand, Brad will take us behind the scenes of human trafficking in Lancaster County. This session will explore how traffickers recruit and control victims, the psychological realities of trauma bonding, and how local task forces respond through both enforcement and prevention. Time will be set aside for questions and dialogue. We’ll be serving a Mai Tai Mocktail as we engage this important and impactful conversation.

title: Virtual Reality Career Exploration
location: Adamstown, ADM Community Room
description:

Join the Adamstown Area Library and Goodwill for a Career Exploration Workshop which includes exploring options for different career fields, what qualities are important at work, and conducting a self-assessment to match interests to careers. The workshop starts at 4:30 PM and is free.This workshop also includes the opportunity to conduct over 50 different jobs in an immersive hands-on Virtual Reality experience. It allows job seekers to experience work in different careers and ultimately get on a path to a well-paying job. Simulations are about 10 minutes long. All are available in Spanish. The job categories include agriculture, architecture and construction, finance, health science, hospitality and tourism, human services, information technology, law and public safety, manufacturing, science and technology, and transportation. Registration is required for this event. This program is for individuals aged 14-25.Your instructor is Lisa Ference, who has a B.S. in Computer Science from Desales University. She is a retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent who investigated computer crimes and intrusions for the FBI in New York City. She now works at Goodwill Keystone Area, providing learning opportunities in the Lehigh Valley and surrounding counties.

Pizza is provided free upstairs. Beer/wine/soda/etc at the bar downstairs!

This months speakers:
**Luke Westfall - *Actually… it IS rocket science ***
At some point, every Kerbal engineer gets tired of manually throttling up and watching their rocket cartwheel into the ocean. In this talk, we'll use Kerbal Space Program, a beloved space flight simulator where failure is half the fun, as a playground for exploring two approaches to automation: the onboard scripting of kOS and the external control API of kRPC. Along the way, we'll discover what they can teach us about flight dynamics, control loops, and why sometimes the best debugging session involves a tiny green astronaut.

**Ken Richards - *Walk Up Song ***
Come see if Ken’s app can guess your age and pick a song you’ll vibe to. Then stick around — he’ll share the creative story, lessons on large vs. small models, and where AI can fall short.

title: The Temptations & The Four Tops
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $79 $89 $99 $109
 
This event was originally scheduled for Thursday, April 9. 
Often referred to as American Music Royalty, The Temptations are world-renowned superstars of entertainment, revered for their phenomenal catalog of music and prolific career.  Thanks to their fine-tuned choreography, and even finer harmonies, The Temptations became one of the most successful acts to record for Motown Records.  During the group’s six-decade career, these Grammy winners have charted numerous #1 hits including “My Girl,” “Ain’t Too Proud to Beg,” “Get Ready,” “Just My Imagination,” and “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone,” among many others. 
The Four Tops teamed up in high school and spent over four decades without a single personnel change to become one of Motown’s most consistent hit makers.  “Baby I Need Your Loving,” “I Can’t Help Myself (Sugar Pie, Honey Bunch),” “Reach Out (I’ll Be There),” “Standing in the Shadows of Love,” and “Ain’t No Woman (Like the One I’ve Got)” are just some of their classic hits. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
June 27, July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:

Discover the amazing world of animals by looking at what’s inside! Animals with a sturdy backbone and a skeleton are called vertebrates, like leaping frogs, soaring birds, and even you.On the flip side, invertebrates are the "spineless" superstars of nature—like wiggly worms and crunchy beetles—who make up almost all the animals on Earth! With powerhouse vocals, undeniable stage presence, and a string of chart-topping hits, Jo Dee Messina remains one of country music’s most vibrant and beloved artists. From the moment she burst onto the scene with “Heads Carolina, Tails California,” Jo Dee has delivered anthems that defined an era and continue to connect with fans across generations. 
Her impressive career includes timeless favorites like “I’m Alright,” “Bye-Bye,” “Lesson in Leavin’,” and “Stand Beside Me,” along with multiple Platinum albums and CMA and ACM Award wins. Known for her high-energy shows and heartfelt storytelling, Jo Dee’s live performances are a celebration of life, love, and resilience. 
The Bennett Hall Band is a rising country trio made up of sisters Kat, Presley, and Josie Hall, whose musical journey began at a young age and continues to captivate audiences across the country. Named in honor of their brother Bennett, the band blends heartfelt storytelling, tight sibling harmonies, and impressive musicianship into an authentic and energetic live performance. 
Kat and Presley began singing together as young children, quickly developing a natural harmony that became the foundation of their sound. Kat soon added guitar and songwriting, while Presley’s perfect pitch found a home on the keys. The youngest sister, Josie, brings vibrant energy on drums, ukulele, and percussion, rounding out the trio’s dynamic stage presence. 
With experience performing on renowned stages throughout Tennessee and beyond—including CMA Fest, The Station Inn, and the Franklin Main Street Festival—The Bennett Hall Band is quickly making its mark on the country music scene with talent, heart, and a sound well beyond their years.

Lauren Daigle is a multi-GRAMMY®-winning, chart-topping vocalist whose powerful, soulful sound has captivated audiences around the globe. With more than a billion streams worldwide and sold-out tours spanning North America, Europe, Australia, and Africa, she has graced some of the world’s most iconic stages, from Carnegie Hall and Red Rocks to Radio City Music Hall, the New Orleans Jazz Fest, and Lollapalooza. She has also performed on one of the world’s biggest stages, singing “America the Beautiful” at the Super Bowl alongside Trombone Shorty. 
Her breakthrough album Look Up Child (2x platinum) debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard Top 200 and made history as Daigle became the first female artist to simultaneously land in the Top 10 of both the Pop and Christian album charts. The album’s 6x platinum hit single “You Say” became one of the longest-running No. 1 songs in Billboard chart history. 
Daigle’s GRAMMY®-nominated self-titled album features standout tracks including “Thank God I Do,” “These Are the Days,” and “Be Okay,” and fueled her wildly successful Kaleidoscope Tour and Kaleidoscope Nights, which played to packed arenas and was extended by popular demand. title: Straight No Chaser: Beach Bash
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $69 $79 $89 
 
If the phrase “male a cappella group” conjures up an image of students in blue blazers, ties, and khakis singing traditional college songs on ivied campuses… think again. Straight No Chaser (SNC) are neither strait-laced nor straight-faced, but neither are they vaudeville-style kitsch. They have emerged as a phenomenon with a massive fanbase and a long list of accomplishments including 2 RIAA Gold Certified albums, over 1.5 million concert tickets sold, over 1 billion streams on Pandora, and over 2 million albums sold worldwide. Straight No Chaser is the real deal, the captivating sound of nine unadulterated human voices coming together to make extraordinary music that is moving people in a fundamental sense… and with a sense of humor. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

Thousands of people come to the village of Bird-in-Hand for the auction which is held on the Smucker Homestead. Equine and antique enthusiasts, consignors, local residents, out-of-town visitors, and whole families look forward to our auction each year. Many are from the East Coast, but also from places as far away as Texas and California. 
This is a significant fundraiser for our Hand-in-Hand Fire Company. We are appreciative of the amazing support we receive both from our local volunteers and the visitors to our area who come back year after year.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:

AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, January 21 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, January 23 at 10:00 a.m. 
Legendary band, THREE DOG NIGHT, now in its 6th decade, claims some of the most astonishing statistics in popular music. In the years 1969 through 1974, no other group achieved more top 10 hits, moved more records, or sold more concert tickets than THREE DOG NIGHT. 
THREE DOG NIGHT hits weave through the fabric of pop culture today, whether on the radio where they are heard day in and day out, in TV commercials or in major motion pictures — songs like “Mama Told Me (Not To Come)”, “Joy to the World”, “Black and White”, “Shambala” and “One” serve to heighten our emotions and crystallize THREE DOG NIGHT’s continuing popularity. 
Boasting chart and sales records that remain virtually unmatched in popular music, THREE DOG NIGHT holds a Billboard Magazine record for releasing 21 consecutive Top 40 hits, including 3 #1 singles “Mama Told Me (Not to Come)”, “Joy to the World”, and “Liar; the chart success drove 7 Platinum-selling singles and 12 straight RIAA Certified Gold LPs. The hits appeared on best-selling charts in all genres (pop, rock, rhythm & blues, and country). Its records continue to sell around the world, reaching beyond the borders of the U.S. into Japan, Canada, Holland, England, Germany, Spain and elsewhere. Tens of millions of THREE DOG NIGHT records have been sold through the years.

title: Terry Fator Pure Imagination: Once Upon a Voice
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $49 $69 $79 $89
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, January 14 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, January 16 at 10:00 a.m. 
Legendary Las Vegas headliner Terry Fator has created a new road show to kickoff his 2025-2026 tour.  Pure Imagination: Once Upon a Voice is a 90 minute spectacular, featuring the incredible impressions, comedy and ventriloquism that has made Terry and his characters a must see show for fans across the nation. 
“Pure Imagination is a totally different concept than my road shows in the past,” Fator said. “I found that throughout my life my imagination had spawned countless characters, song parodies and comedy skits and I compiled them all together to give my audience a fun look into my creative psyche.” 
The show features the classic characters Terry has made famous over the years: Winston the Impersonating Turtle; Country Star Walter T. Airdale; Apollo Theater legend Julius; perpetual slacker and stoner Duggie; Vikki the Cougar and the world’s greatest Elvis impersonator, Maynard Tompkins. 
“One idea I had is to add in characters and impressions based on real-life stars people around the world know and love,” Fator said.  “So you can look forward to seeing and hearing Willie Nelson, Michael Jackson, Justin Bieber, plus a few surprise ‘guests’”. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

She was also the only UK finalist in the global #SearchForDolly casting search for Dolly’s Broadway musical. 
More than a tribute, Kelly delivers a true illusion. With a pitch-perfect Tennessee accent, soaring soprano vocals, and the warmth, wit, and charm that define Dolly, she captures not just the look—but the spirit—of the Queen of Country. Audiences leave feeling uplifted, entertained, and convinced they’ve experienced something truly special. 
Backed by a live band, The Dolly Show is a dazzling, full-scale theatrical concert featuring Dolly’s greatest hits from the 1960s to today, including “Jolene,” “9 to 5,” “Islands in the Stream,” and “I Will Always Love You.” Expect powerhouse vocals, laugh-out-loud moments, rhinestone-studded glamour, and heartfelt storytelling throughout the evening. 
An award-winning performer with an international career spanning television, musical theatre, and live music, Kelly O’Brien has captivated audiences around the globe and appeared on major outlets including BBC One, ITV’s This Morning, Lorraine, Channel 5, and Sky. 
From the iconic silhouette to the signature Southern charm, Kelly O’Brien is Dolly—bringing one of music’s most treasured legends to life in a show that’s as joyful as it is unforgettable.

Aaron Lewis, the Vermont-born powerhouse first found success with Staind–the 2000s-era hard-rockers who injected meditative muscle into an era better known for mindless aggression. But while that band is still very much alive, it was never enough to satisfy Lewis’ creative drive. 
Embracing his roots to earn a rare second round of success, a series of solo country projects have led to two No. 1 Billboard Country Album debuts–TOWN LINE (2011) and SINNER(2016)–plus a PLATINUM collab with heroes George Jones and Charlie Daniels (“Country Boy”), and a GOLD-certified Billboard No. 1 with “Am I The Only One” in 2021. description:

Public On-Sale: Friday, April 17 at 10:00 a.m. 
Patty Griffin, a two-time GRAMMY® Award winner and one of the most influential singer-songwriters of her generation, brings her deeply personal and emotionally rich music to the stage. Celebrated for her masterful storytelling and soulful voice, Griffin has spent over two decades crafting songs that explore love, loss, identity, and the shared experiences that connect us all. 
Blending folk, Americana, and blues, her music resonates with honesty and depth. Her latest album, Crown of Roses, is an intimate and introspective collection born from a period of reflection, offering songs that speak to resilience, transformation, and embracing new truths. Experience an evening with an artist whose songs linger long after the final note. 
Kathleen Edwards is a modern-day cornerstone of North American roots music. Since making her debut with 2002’s Failer, she’s spent the 21st century occupying the grey area between genres, swirling together her own mix of alt-country, folk, and heartland rock & roll. It’s a sound that has earned its creator more than a half-dozen Juno nominations, shows with icons like Bob Dylan and Willie Nelson, and Top 40 success on both sides of the Canadian/American border. From co-writes with Maren Morris to critically-acclaimed solo records like Back to Me, Asking for Flowers, Voyageur, and Total Freedom, Edwards has become a leader of the Americana community, even as her ever-evolving music reaches beyond the format’s boundaries.

Relive the soundtrack of a generation when Tommy James & The Shondells take the stage for a night of nonstop hits and pure nostalgia. With an incredible string of chart-topping classics, this legendary group helped define the sound of the late ’60s and early ’70s — and their music continues to ignite audiences around the world. 
Sing along to iconic favorites like “Crimson and Clover,” “Mony Mony,” “I Think We’re Alone Now,” “Hanky Panky,” and “Mirage.” Packed with unforgettable melodies, driving rhythms, and timeless pop-rock energy, this concert delivers hit after hit in a high-octane live performance that spans decades of musical history. 
Whether you grew up with these songs on the radio or discovered them through movies, commercials, and modern covers, Tommy James & The Shondells bring a feel-good evening of classic rock that’s perfect for fans of all ages. Don’t miss your chance to experience these legendary songs performed live — a night of memories, music, and pure fun awaits.

title: The Beach Boys: Saluting 60 Years of Pet Sounds
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $79 $99 $119
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Thursday, February 26 at 9:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, February 27 at 10:00 a.m. 
  
As The Beach Boys mark more than a half century of making music, the group continues to ride the crest of a wave unequalled in America’s musical history. The Beach Boys – who have become synonymous with the California lifestyle and an American icon to fans around the world – are bringing “The Sounds of Summer” tour to cities around the globe. 
Since the band’s co-founder, lead-singer and chief lyricist Mike Love penned the lyrics to The Beach Boys’ first hit,“Surfin’” (1961), dozens of the bands chart toppers have become eternal anthems of American youth: “Surfin’ USA,” “Surfer Girl,” “Fun, Fun, Fun,” “I Get Around,” “California Girls,” “Help Me Rhonda,” “Barbara Ann,” “Good Vibrations,” “Wouldn’t It Be Nice,” “Rock and Roll Music” and “Kokomo.” 
The Beach Boys have sold over 100 million records worldwide and have received more than 33 RIAA Platinum and Gold record awards. The Rock And Roll Hall of Famers where also honored at the 2001 Grammy Awards with the Lifetime Achievement Award. With more than five decades of touring under their belts, The Beach Boys have performed more concerts than any major rock band in history. 
The Beach Boys are led by legendary Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, Grammy® winner, New York Times best-selling author, co-founder, lead singer, chief lyricist of The Beach Boys, and 2025 Songwriters Hall of Fame inductee, Mike Love, who, along with musical director Brian Eichenberger, Christian Love, Tim Bonhomme, Jon Bolton, Keith Hubacher, Randy Leago and John Wedemeyer continue the legacy of the iconic band. 
In 2026, The Beach Boys are celebrating 250 years of the USA while saluting The 60th Anniversary of Pet Sounds.

Spend an inspiring evening with Jeremy Camp, one of contemporary Christian music’s most influential and enduring artists. Known for his powerful blend of worship and rock, Camp has spent more than two decades creating music that connects deeply with audiences through messages of hope, perseverance, and faith. 
With chart-topping songs like “I Still Believe,” “Walk by Faith,” and “There Will Be a Day,” his live performances are both uplifting and deeply personal—bringing together heartfelt storytelling and dynamic musicianship. 
Camp’s impact on Christian music has earned him widespread recognition, including multiple GMA Dove Awards—with wins for New Artist of the Year and Male Vocalist of the Year—along with numerous additional nominations across his career. He has also received American Music Award nominations for Favorite Contemporary Inspirational Artist and a Grammy Award nomination for Best Pop/Contemporary Gospel Album. 
Backed by a talented band and delivered with authenticity, this concert offers an evening of meaningful music and connection. Whether you’ve followed his career for years or are discovering his music for the first time, Jeremy Camp’s live performance is an experience that leaves a lasting impression.

location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $34 $39 
Ben & Rose are more than just a duo — they’re a harmony born of Lancaster County’s Plain Community, where tradition, faith, and family shape every note. Their music carries the quiet strength of country roads and the timeless beauty of rural life, weaving humility and heart into every song. Blending country, folk, and gospel, Ben & Rose create music that is both tender and timeless. Their young voices lock together like old friends, evoking front-porch evenings, Sunday hymns, and the kind of stories that linger long after the last note. Each performance is a reminder that simple living can yield the richest music — songs filled with love, hope, and the rhythms of everyday grace. 
Their journey began as teenagers singing side by side, finding harmonies to Lady Antebellum tracks at local youth gatherings. What started at karaoke nights grew into something far deeper: a loving marriage and a shared passion for storytelling through song. Today, their harmonies carry the same spark of those early days, polished by years of life, love, and laughter together. 
Ben & Rose often collaborate with fellow Plain Community songwriter Conrad Fisher, whose work has been recorded by legends like the Oak Ridge Boys, Rhonda Vincent, and The Malpass Brothers. Together, they craft music that feels both rooted and refreshing — a modern echo of simpler times, celebrating the beauty found in everyday life.

Known for his signature blend of heartfelt ballads and high-energy anthems, Morgan has built a career rooted in real-life experiences, patriotism, and a deep connection to his fans. His chart-topping hits include “Redneck Yacht Club,” “That’s What I Love About Sunday,” “International Harvester,” and “Almost Home,” songs that capture the spirit of everyday life with honesty and heart. 
Before his rise in country music, Morgan proudly served in the U.S. Army, a background that continues to shape both his music and his character. His dedication to service and community has earned him widespread respect, including recognition from organizations supporting military members and veterans. 
On stage, Craig Morgan delivers a powerful live show filled with energy, humor, and genuine connection. Whether he’s sharing stories behind his songs or leading the crowd in a singalong, his performances feel as personal as they are entertaining.

title: The Great American Tour
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $59 $69 $79
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, February 11 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, February 13 at 10:00 a.m. 
The Great American Tour is a celebration of the timeless music that defined a generation—and continues to resonate today. Baby Boomers have never lost their passion for the “oldies but goodies” of the 1960s and 70s, and this unforgettable show delivers the songs that shaped youth, freedom, and the unifying power of rock ’n roll. Featuring iconic artists inducted into the Vocal Group Hall of Fame, this tour brings together legendary performers whose hits remain woven into modern movies, television, and commercials, captivating audiences across generations. 
Headlining the tour are Jay and the Americans, one of the era’s few groups still featuring two original members. With an incredible legacy that includes 19 charted hits and 9 Top 40 records, the group continues to thrive with over 900,000 monthly Spotify listeners. Their smash hit “Come a Little Bit Closer”—famously featured in Guardians of the Galaxy—has amassed more than 190 million streams, while classics like “This Magic Moment,” “Cara Mia,” “Walkin’ in the Rain,” and “Only in America” remain beloved fan favorites. 
Joining them are The Classics IV, renowned for their instantly recognizable sound and million-selling, Gold Disc–winning hits “Spooky,” “Traces,” and “Stormy.” Also appearing are Vocal Group Hall of Fame inductees Jay Siegel’s Tokens, led by original frontman Jay Siegel, still thrilling audiences with soaring falsettos on classics such as “Tonight I Fell In Love,” “I Hear Trumpets Blow,” and the immortal “The Lion Sleeps Tonight,” a song continually rediscovered through The Lion King on Broadway and film. 
Perfect for audiences eager to relive cherished memories—or introduce younger generations to the music that started it all—The Great American Tour delivers enduring hits with heart, harmony, and history.

title: A Bronx Tale: One Man Show Starring Chazz Palminteri
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $49 $59 $79
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, May 6 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, May 8 at 10:00 a.m. 
Bronx-born and raised Chazz Palminteri wrote A Bronx Tale in 1988. The powerful one-man stage play depicted his bruising childhood which included witnessing a gangland killing when he was nine years old. Palminteri played 18 characters and brought them all to life in his autobiographical play. His friends, enemies and family came alive on stage. Hollywood Studios went crazy after seeing it and offered him millions of dollars to turn it into a major movie. There was one catch… They wanted to put a star in the role of Sonny and someone else to write the screenplay. With $200 dollars in the bank…Palminteri said No… he would hold out and wait. He wanted to play Sonny and write the screenplay. Then one night, Palminteri walked into his dressing room and siting there was Robert De Niro who just saw the show… He said it was the greatest one-man show he’s ever seen. Robert DeNiro gave Palminteri the chance he was waiting for… And as they say in Hollywood the rest is history.  Palminteri wrote the screenplay for the film A Bronx Tale and then most recently wrote the book for the Broadway Musical. It was the first time in history that the same actor wrote the one-man play, the movie, and the Broadway Musical and starred in each one. The show you will see now is the exact show Chazz Palminteri did 34 years ago with just a chair that made him a star.

title: Bird-in-Hand Hot Air Balloon Festival
location: Bird-in-Hand Event Field, 320 North Ronks Road, Bird-in-Hand, 17505, United States
description:
We’re taking our favorite high-flying, family-friendly fun fall event to new heights! 
We’re thrilled to partner with Balloon Shows USA to bring you an all-new balloon festival. Enjoy a weekend of spectacular hot air balloon glows and laser light shows, music, family activities, food trucks, craft vendors and more. 
You’ll find lots to do in the afternoon and evening. Ascend in a tethered balloon, weather permitting. Browse our retailers’ offerings. If you’re bringing little ones, take a wagon ride, visit our kids’ area, and let them burn off some energy in the bounce houses. Grab a bite to eat from our food trucks; each will offer a special bacon-themed dish in addition to its regular menu. 
At 8:30, the lights come on and the fun kicks into high gear. Watch as massive tethered hot air balloons illuminate the night and state-of-the-art laser displays paint the sky with brilliant colors. It’s an unforgettable sight and an experience you won’t want to miss. 
What to expect: 

Massive balloons and special shaped balloons guaranteed to delight kids and adults alike.
Check your bucket list and get a ride in a real tethered balloon ($35, weather permitting).
High-energy entertainment all evening with our DJ.
Shop, explore and discover craft and retail vendors with unique finds and handmade goods.
Satisfy your cravings at our food truck festival, featuring special bacon-themed creations from select vendors.
Take in the scenery and enjoy our farm with free hayrides.
Don’t miss the Kids Zone with games, rides, bounce houses and nonstop fun ($5 to $20 for unlimited rides).
The Grand Finale (8:30 pm nightly) with Balloon Glow & Laser Show, music and synchronized balloon burn, giant glowing balloons and crowd countdowns

Dates: Friday, September 25, 2026 & Saturday, September 26, 2026
Time: 3 pm–10 pm both days
Grand Finale: 8:30 pm 
Tickets:  
In advance
VIP: $45/day
Adults: $25/day
Kids (6-12): $15/day
Kids (5 and under): FREE 
Tickets will be available at the gate for an additional cost. 
Get tickets now before we sell out. 
Click here to order tickets

This activity is FREE with your paid admission or membership to the Lancaster Science Factory.

title: First Friday @ The Lancaster Science Factory!
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Every First Friday the Lancaster Science Factory offers free admission from 5 – 7pm for the first 300 guests. Explore over 80 interactive exhibits for kids in grades K – 8 and their families! This program is possible through the generous support of PPL. 
  
CHILDREN MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY AN ADULT
